title: Isaiah (Part 4) — The Suffering Servant
hook: God never filed the paperwork. That's the startling legal detail buried in Isaiah 50:1—Israel assumes she's been divorced, cast off for good, but the Lord asks pointedly: where is the certificate? Under Mosaic law a husband needed a formal document to sever covenant, and God produces none, because He never initiated the separation at all. That single unanswered question sets the tone for everything that follows in these chapters—a people convinced they've been abandoned, met again and again by a God who keeps circling back with summons to wake up, sing, and come buy wine and milk without money. And right in the middle of it all sits Isaiah 53, the servant despised and stricken, bearing grief no one expected to recognize as salvation. Spend time this week with a God who answers accusation not with defensiveness but with invitation—you may find the "bill of divorcement" you've been looking for was never written in the first place.
